body.statement: Under the same one-observation law with \(p_n=p\) fixed before \(n\to\infty\), the true-propensity IPW and oracle DR bulk-coordinate gradient variances at \(\beta=0\) are \(1/8\) and \(v_\gamma/4\), respectively. On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), the exact linear entropy-balance variance is \(1/16\); this event has probability tending to one in the fixed-dimensional limit. Consequently, as \(\kappa\downarrow0\) after the proportional limits, \(r_T=\kappa/(4\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), \(r_E=\kappa/(8\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), and \(r_D=v_\gamma\kappa/(2\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), provided the certified-event uniform remainder asserted by the joint system holds. The uniform complement-event fallback is not identified with entropy balancing in this reduction.
body.justification: This sanity reduction anchors the proportional system to the classical HIR projection while showing that linear balance remains strictly short of oracle DR when \(\gamma>0\).
body.gap: HiranoImbensRidder2003 and FangRidderXie2026 obtain full efficiency from sufficiently rich estimated propensity scores; the exact same-coordinate linear balance used here spans only a partial projection.
body.consumer: The reduction gives analysts a low-dimensional diagnostic and prevents interpreting exact linear balance as automatic oracle efficiency.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniform control that permits taking the proportional deterministic limit first and then sending the aspect ratio to zero for the original same-sample entropy estimator.
obligation.obstruction: Fixed-dimensional asymptotic linearity controls each fixed number of coordinates but does not control the sum of a growing number of coordinate errors. The needed uniform remainder is part of the unresolved joint system and cannot be inferred from the frozen assumptions.
obligation.attempted: All three fixed-dimensional influence functions, bulk-coordinate variances, and fixed-dimensional feasibility were proved, and the claimed small-aspect-ratio coefficients were recovered algebraically under the missing uniform remainder.
obligation.partial_result:
For every fixed bulk coordinate \(k>1\), the fixed-dimensional gradient influence variances are rigorously
\[
 s_T=\frac18,
 \qquad s_E=\frac1{16},
 \qquad s_D=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]
The common local negative Hessian is \(\lambda I_p/4\), and \(g(r)=r^2/8+o(r^2)\).  Therefore, if a proportional deterministic equivalent admits a remainder uniform as \(\kappa\downarrow0\), its algebraic first-order coefficient must be
\[
 r_j=\frac{2s_j}{\lambda}\kappa+o(\kappa),
\]
which gives the three coefficients in the target.  The required interchange between the proportional limit and \(\kappa\downarrow0\) is not implied by fixed-dimensional asymptotic linearity.
